title: ERP / Oracle APEX model shortlist

coding.plain: How good it is at writing code.

agentic.plain: How well it works through a multi-step job using tools.

lcr.plain: How well it keeps track of a very long document.

nh.plain: How often it admits it does not know instead of inventing an answer.

acc.plain: How often its answer is simply right.

code_mig.plain: How well it rewrites an old program in another language.

corpfin.plain: How well it answers questions about long contracts.

pass1.plain: How often it fixes a real bug on the first try.

task_cost.plain: What one finished task costs, in dollars.
task_cost.label: DeepSWE cost per task

price.label: Blended price per 1M tokens, 3:1 input to output

e2e.plain: Seconds until the whole answer is there.
e2e.label: End-to-end response time, median

ttft.plain: Seconds until the first word appears.
ttft.label: Time to first token, median

steps.plain: How many turns it needs to finish one task.
steps.label: DeepSWE agent turns per task

dur.plain: How long one task runs, in seconds.
dur.label: DeepSWE task duration

roles.name: Batch migration
roles.note: Long unattended runs converting Forms and PL/SQL. Code Migration is the closest public proxy.

roles.name: Interactive edit loop
roles.note: Page-edit turnaround, where waiting costs a developer more than tokens do.

roles.name: Quality only
roles.note: Model quality with cost and speed removed, for work where correctness dominates.

gaps: Claude Fable 5.1 has no DeepSWE row. The site lists only claude-fable-5, a different model, so pass@1 and cost per task are empty rather than borrowed.
Muse Spark 1.3 and Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B carry no Code Migration row, so neither gets a batch score.
CorpFin v2 covers 134 models and excludes GPT-6 Astra, Muse Spark 1.3, Gemini 3.8 Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash and Claude Fable 5.1. It feeds no role index and is reported as context only.
Artificial Analysis Agentic Index coverage fell from 197 models to 119 between the 20260904 and 20260906 scrapes, which moved agentic scores across the whole candidate set.

glossary.TTFT: Time to first token: seconds from sending the request until the first output token arrives. For Anthropic and OpenAI models this includes hidden reasoning time.
glossary.E2E: End-to-end response time: median seconds from request to complete answer (Artificial Analysis).
glossary.AA-LCR: Artificial Analysis Long Context Reasoning, 0-1. Proxy for handling large schemas and long packages.
glossary.Code Migration: Vals AI benchmark: reimplement real programs in another language (CLI, COBOL, code quality subtasks). Private set, 0-100, published with stderr.
glossary.CorpFin v2: Vals AI benchmark: reasoning over long corporate credit agreements. 0-100, with stderr.
glossary.Non-halluc: AA-Omniscience non-hallucination rate, 0-1: share of unknown questions where the model declines instead of inventing an answer.
glossary.non-hallucination: AA-Omniscience non-hallucination rate, 0-1: share of unknown questions where the model declines instead of inventing an answer.
glossary.acc: AA-Omniscience accuracy, 0-1: share of questions answered correctly. Read together with non-hallucination: high refusal plus low accuracy means the model abstains rather than knows.
glossary.Agentic: Artificial Analysis Agentic Index, 0-100: multi-step, tool-using tasks.
glossary.$/1M: Artificial Analysis blended price per 1M tokens at a 3:1 input:output ratio.
glossary.$/task: DeepSWE v1.1 mean USD per completed task, thinking tokens included.
glossary.DeepSWE: Datacurve's long-horizon software engineering benchmark: 113 tasks across 91 repositories, every model run under the mini-swe-agent scaffold.
glossary.mini-swe-agent: The single agent scaffold DeepSWE uses for every model.
glossary.IFBench: Instruction-following benchmark reported by Artificial Analysis, 0-1.
glossary.Intelligence Index: Artificial Analysis composite of knowledge, reasoning, coding and agentic evals, 0-100.
glossary.Artificial Analysis: Independent model benchmark and pricing tracker (artificialanalysis.ai).
glossary.max effort: Reasoning effort setting on Artificial Analysis. Higher effort spends more thinking tokens; per-token price stays flat, cost per task does not.
glossary.xhigh: Reasoning effort one step below max, as Artificial Analysis names it.
